Only sr3-01 is flagged. The other 11 pass, each confirmed by a quote and against the spec:

- sr3-03 (video first frame versus poster): web.dev says the poster image load time or first frame presentation time is used, "whichever is earlier". - sr3-05 (full-viewport exclusion): web.dev lists it as a Chromium heuristic. The W3C spec now makes it normative too ("If size is equal to rootWidth times rootHeight, return null"). The Chromium wording is still correct.

cards.statement: Under font-display: block, the browser shows fallback text if the web font is still loading after the block period.
cards.explanation: block gives a short block period and an infinite swap period: text stays invisible only briefly, then a fallback font shows it until the web font arrives and swaps in.
cards.reason: The wording lens's objection holds. In the fallback version the value's name gives away the True answer, and it tests the same late-font outcome as sr10-05 (optional). I used the wording lens's replacement and checked it on MDN font-display: "block: Gives the font face a short block period and an infinite swap period" and swap period: "any element attempting to use it must render a fallback font face". It gives no durations, the name 'block' points a guesser toward False, and r10 keeps the same number of true cards. Source changes to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@font-face/font-display (title: font-display).

cards.statement: web.dev cites Web Almanac data in which sites using third-party fonts rendered faster than self-hosting sites.
cards.explanation: web.dev says the Web Almanac saw faster renders with third-party fonts and that self-hosted fonts are much less likely to win without a CDN and HTTP/2.
cards.reason: Merged the two lenses. The wording lens is right that the CDN/HTTP/2 advice is close to a truism, so the less obvious Web Almanac finding becomes the statement and the advice moves to the explanation. Both quotes confirmed on web.dev/articles/font-best-practices (updated 2022-10-04): "sites using third-party fonts had a faster render than fonts that used first-party fonts" and "Without use of these technologies, it's much less likely that self-hosted fonts deliver better performance." Credited to web.dev, so it stays stable.

cards.statement: Replacing a file at the same URL on the server makes the browser refetch it while its cached copy is still fresh.
cards.explanation: The browser reuses a cached response until it is no longer fresh. web.dev puts a fingerprint or version in the file name, so changed content gets a new URL.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. 'At the same URL' removes the versioned-URL ambiguity, and the web.dev HTTP cache quotes support both freshness and fingerprinting.

cards.statement: web.dev treats a page whose window.opener is non-null as a safe candidate for the bfcache.
cards.explanation: web.dev says a page with a non-null window.opener can't safely enter the bfcache, because pages trying to access it could break; rel="noopener" avoids creating the reference.
cards.reason: Fact and answer kept. The fact lens's style note holds: the editor's statement repeated web.dev's sentence with only "can't safely" changed to "is safe", which breaks the rule against copying a source sentence with a word or two changed. I reworded it without changing the fact. Confirmed on web.dev/articles/bfcache: "a page with a non-null window.opener reference can't safely be put into bfcache, because that could break any pages attempting to access it", with rel="noopener" advised.

cards.statement: CSS upscaling makes an LCP image's reported area larger than the image's intrinsic area.
cards.explanation: LCP compensates for image upscaling, so CSS enlargement does not let the reported area exceed the image's intrinsic area.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. The 'lets' tell is removed. The W3C LCP spec divides size by scaleFactor when it is greater than 1, so the reported area cannot exceed the natural area.

cards.statement: With unicode-range, the browser downloads the matching glyphs of a font as a partial file.
cards.explanation: unicode-range decides whether a font face is needed: MDN says if the page uses one character in the range, the whole font is downloaded. Byte savings come from separate subset files.
cards.reason: Applied the fact lens's fix: the old phrase 'triggers the whole file' never said what is triggered. Confirmed on MDN unicode-range: "if it uses at least one, the whole font is downloaded" and that the descriptor exists so font resources can be segmented. The statement and answer are unchanged.

cards.statement: A client advertises the compression formats it accepts in a Content-Encoding request header.
cards.explanation: Content-Encoding identifies the coding applied to a representation. Accept-Encoding communicates the client's acceptable codings.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it and the 'lets' tell is removed. The partial hint from sr11-09 is a deck-level issue this rewrite did not cause.

cards.statement: LCP counts a text block's CSS padding as part of its candidate area.
cards.explanation: LCP sizes text using the bounds of its text nodes, excluding CSS padding, borders, and margins.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. web.dev LCP: "LCP doesn't consider margins, paddings, or borders applied using CSS." The 'X includes Y' template is broken.

cards.statement: LCP resource load duration covers the wait to display an image after its download finishes.
cards.explanation: Waiting after the LCP resource finishes loading belongs to element render delay, not resource load duration.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep it. The Chrome LCP breakdown page defines element render delay as the time between the end of the LCP resource load and the element rendering fully. The template tell is removed.
